data.title: Stephen Harper Says Canada Previously Had to Withdraw From U.S. Trade Talks
data.description: According to Wallstreetcn, former Canadian Prime Minister Stephen Harper said Canada previously had to withdraw from trade talks with the United States.

data.title: Rick Pitcairn Cautions Wealthy Clients on SpaceX, Private Markets
data.description:
Rick Pitcairn, chairman and chief global strategist at family office Pitcairn, said it is his job to tap the brakes on wealthy clients who want to put too much money into "shiny star" investments such as SpaceX or private markets, according to Bloomberg.

He said private credit and private markets have a role, but they should be part of a diversified portfolio.

data.title: STOCKS | Baltic Exchange Data Shows Record $44.8 Million Cost to Ship U.S. Gulf Crude to Asia
data.description: According to Wallstreetcn, Baltic Exchange data showed that as of Tuesday, the cost of chartering a very large crude carrier to transport 2 million barrels of U.S. Gulf crude to Asia was about $44.8 million, a record high.

data.title: PRECIOUS METALS | Spot Gold Falls 0.16% in New York Late Trading
data.description: According to Wallstreetcn, spot gold fell 0.16% to $4,292.85 per ounce in New York late trading on Tuesday, September 15, while spot silver rose 0.70% to $63.6661 per ounce and COMEX copper futures gained 0.80% to $6.4545 per pound. The Philadelphia Gold and Silver Index, traded during U.S. stock market hours, closed up 0.01% at 387.64, the NYSE Arca Gold Miners Index fell 0.53% to 2,693.03, and the Materials Index rose 0.37% while the Metals and Mining Index gained 0.14%.

data.title: U.S. Presses Mexico to Accept New AI Hardware Export Rules
data.description:
The U.S. government is pressuring Mexican officials to accept new rules on artificial intelligence hardware exports, according to people familiar with the matter. According to ChainCatcher, trade officials from the two countries are expected to hold another round of talks in Washington as early as next week.

The discussions are also expected to cover the possibility of lowering U.S. tariffs on steel, aluminum, and automobiles.

data.title: Crypto Transactions on Agentic Payment Rails Are Surging
data.description:
Crypto transactions on agentic payment rails are surging. According to Bloomberg, the increase is being driven by AI agents that can make payments on behalf of users.

The article says these rails are designed to let software agents handle transactions, and that activity on them has risen. It also says the trend is tied to the growing use of AI agents in payments.

data.title: AI | Anthropic Expands Finance Ties With BlackRock
data.description:
BlackRock senior managing director Jaime Magyera said advisers are using artificial intelligence to help parse increasingly complex capital markets after Anthropic announced new ties with BlackRock, according to Bloomberg.

Magyera also said AI is helping create more strategic customization for clients.

data.title: ExxonMobil Gets Texas Approval for Rose Carbon-Capture Project
data.description: ExxonMobil Holdings Corp. won approval for its Rose carbon-capture project in Texas in a 2-to-1 vote, according to Bloomberg. The decision allows ExxonMobil to move ahead with the emission-reducing development, which could be among the biggest of its kind.

data.title: Bond Traders Bet Fed Will Extend Treasury Selloff
data.description:
Bond traders have built extreme short positions ahead of Wednesday’s Federal Reserve meeting, betting the Treasury selloff will continue, according to Bloomberg.

The move comes as yields have climbed to their highest levels in more than a decade.

data.title: STOCKS | Mortgage Insurers Fall After FHFA Chief Bill Pulte Hints at Fee Relief
data.description: According to Wallstreetcn, mortgage insurance stocks fell after FHFA Director Bill Pulte suggested that homeowners should not be forced to pay mortgage insurance fees in some cases, with MGIC Investment Corp. down 3.1% for its worst single-day performance since April, Essent Group Ltd. down 0.9%, and Radian Group Inc. and NMI Holdings Inc. both down 1.4%.

data.title: US Treasury Yields Edge Higher After Weak 20-Year Auction Demand
data.description:
U.S. long-dated Treasury prices fell slightly on Tuesday after the 20-year Treasury auction cleared at a yield above pre-sale trading levels, while oil prices rose on supply risks. According to Sina Finance, the 10-year Treasury yield briefly reached 5.04% before easing back below 5% after 3:00 p.m. New York time.

The 10-year yield later rose 1.7 basis points to 5.004% as of 4:32 p.m. U.S. Eastern Time, while the 2-year yield rose 1.6 basis points to 4.6734%, the 5-year yield rose 1.5 basis points to 4.8368%, and the 30-year yield rose 2.2 basis points to 5.3662%. The 5s30s spread widened about 0.7 basis point to 52.76 basis points, and the 2s10s spread widened about 0.3 basis point to 32.85 basis points.

The $13 billion reopening of 20-year U.S. Treasurys cleared at a yield 2 basis points above the pre-sale yield, adding to afternoon steepening pressure on the U.S. yield curve. Bid data were weak, with the primary dealer take-up rising to 16.9%, the highest since February, while indirect bidder take-up fell to 52.5% and direct bidder take-up rose to 30.7%.

In rate options, hedging demand increased around Wednesday's Federal Reserve decision, and the swaps market was almost fully pricing in a 25-basis-point rate hike. Short-term rate contracts also showed demand for upside hedges against a scenario in which the Fed leaves rates unchanged on Wednesday, with the market currently pricing about 23 basis points of tightening. The market also saw demand for short June 2027 SOFR straddles for a third straight session, with the trade having collected about $150 million in premiums.

data.title: AI | BlackRock's Fink Says Delayed Buildout Is Limiting AI Access
data.description:
BlackRock Inc. Chief Executive Officer Larry Fink said delays in the buildout of artificial intelligence are limiting access to the technology for everyone, according to Bloomberg.

He made the remarks at the Canada Investment Summit on Tuesday.

data.title: STOCKS | North American tech software ETF falls 1.02%, cybersecurity ETFs rise
data.description: According to Wallstreetcn, the North American tech software stock index ETF fell 1.02% to $105.55, while the Global X Cybersecurity ETF rose 2.23%, the Nasdaq Cybersecurity ETF gained 0.95%, and the ETFMG Cybersecurity ETF advanced 1.71%.

data.title: AI TRENDS | BitBox Adds Lightning Hot Wallet Support in BitBoxApp
data.description: BitBox now lets owners of any BitBox hardware wallet create a Lightning hot wallet in BitBoxApp. According to NS3.AI, users can fund the wallet from their on-chain balance and pay Lightning invoices without switching apps, wallets, or third-party services. The Lightning wallet uses the existing BitBox backup while remaining separate from the hardware wallet.

data.title: Jan van Eck Says Gold Is Not Driven by US Inflation
data.description:
Jan van Eck, chief executive officer of VanEck Funds, said gold is not driven by US inflation and said he is not worried about the $40 trillion US debt, according to Bloomberg.

Speaking on Bloomberg Businessweek Daily from Future Proof, van Eck said Bessent and US President Donald Trump are "toying" with the market over the idea of sending $5,000 checks to Americans if they keep control of Congress.

data.title: STOCKS | U.S. ETFs Fall Across Equities and Bonds, Brent Oil Fund Rises 2.25%
data.description: According to Wallstreetcn, on Tuesday, September 15, Barclays U.S. Convertible Bond ETF fell 0.91%, the Russell 2000 ETF lost 0.7%, the Nasdaq 100 ETF and Dow ETF fell at least 0.62%, the long yen ETF fell 0.5%, the S&P 500 ETF fell 0.46%, the emerging markets ETF fell 0.35%, and the agricultural products fund, U.S. 20+ year Treasury ETF, U.S. real estate ETF, and long euro ETF fell as much as 0.28%, while the long U.S. dollar index ETF rose 0.18%, the gold ETF gained 0.33%, the soybeans fund rose 0.94%, and the U.S. Brent oil fund climbed 2.25%.

data.title: Ethereum Polymarket Odds for $2,600 Breakout Jump to 73.5%
data.description: Polymarket odds for the Ethereum September price prediction market’s "break above $2,600" outcome rose sharply to 73.5% from 50% one hour earlier, according to Catcher Predict monitoring. According to ChainCatcher, the move reflected a 23.5 percentage point swing and came amid a reported impact from breaking news.

data.title: Anthropic's Amodei And Nvidia's Huang Clash Over AI Safety At Salesforce Dreamforce
data.description: According to CNBC, Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei and Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang offered contrasting views on artificial intelligence safety at Salesforce's Dreamforce conference in San Francisco, where Salesforce also announced a new reasoning model for its Agentforce platform built on one of Nvidia's open-weight Nemotron models. Amodei, speaking with Salesforce CEO Marc Benioff, said the industry should set an example and slow the pace of model development, while Huang argued that market forces already provide discipline and that speed and safety can coexist. Benioff said companies should slow down or speed up as they see fit, but should be held accountable. Salesforce and Anthropic also expanded their strategic partnership late last month and unveiled Claudeforce, a new way for salespeople to access data directly inside Anthropic's Claude chatbot.

data.title: Bitcoin Falls 4% as Senate Blocks Clarity Act
data.description:
The Senate blocked the Clarity Act after the bill received 49 votes for and 50 against, falling short of the 60 votes needed to advance. According to NS3.AI, the proposal would divide oversight of digital assets among regulators and classify them as securities, commodities or stablecoins.

Bitcoin traded at $75,997 after falling 4% in 24 hours. U.S. President Donald Trump urged lawmakers to pass the bill last month.

data.title: AI TRENDS | Salesforce CEO Marc Benioff on AI Safety: Enterprises and Tech Executives Must Be Held Accountable
data.description: According to Wallstreetcn, Salesforce Chief Executive Officer Marc Benioff said at a Salesforce event that enterprises and technology executives must be held accountable for the technology they develop.
